Three equal masses $m$ are kept at vertices $(A,B,C)$ of an equilateral triangle of side a in free space. At $t=0$, they are given an initial velocity $V_{A}\leftarrow =V_{0}AC\leftarrow ,V_{B}\leftarrow =V_{0}BA\leftarrow$ and $V_{C}\leftarrow =V_{0}CB\leftarrow$. Here, $AC\leftarrow ,CB\leftarrow$ and $BA\leftarrow$ are unit vectors along the edges of the triangle. If the three masses interact gravitationally, then the magnitude of the net angular momentum of the system at the point of collision is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The gravitational forces between the masses are internal, so the net external torque about any fixed point is zero and the total angular momentum of the system about that point stays the same up to the collision.

Take moments about the fixed point C at $t=0$:


[IMG]

Mass at A moves along AC, a line passing through C, so its angular momentum about C is zero.

Mass at C is at the reference point, so its angular momentum about C is zero.

Mass at B moves along BA with speed $V_{0}$. The perpendicular distance of line AB from C is the altitude $\sqrt{a^{2}-\dfrac{a^{2}}{4}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a$, so its angular momentum about C has magnitude $mV_{0}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a$.

$L=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}amV_{0}$

and this is also the magnitude of the net angular momentum at the collision.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: In an experiment with photoelectric effect, the stopping potential,
options: is $\left (\frac{1}{e}\right )$ times the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons
increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
decreases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
increases with increase in the wavelength of the incident light
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $eV_{0}=hv-𝜙$ .... (i)

$\Rightarrow eV_{0}=KE_{\max }$ (where $𝜙$ = work function of the metal and $V_{0}$ = stopping potential)

$\Rightarrow V_{0}=\left (\frac{1}{e}\right )KE_{\max }$

Stopping potential depends solely on the frequency of the incident light $(v)$ & the work function of the metal, not the intensity.

From eq. (i), we can see,

$v↑\Rightarrow v_{0}↑$

$\Rightarrow \frac{c}{λ↓}\Rightarrow v_{0}↑$ (as $v=\frac{c}{λ}$)

So, stopping potential increases with decrease in the wavelength of the incident light.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

text: The difference of temperature in a material can convert heat energy into electrical energy. To harvest the heat energy, the material should have
options: low thermal conductivity and high electrical conductivity
low thermal conductivity and low electrical conductivity
high thermal conductivity and high electrical conductivity
high thermal conductivity and low electrical conductivity
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To convert a temperature difference into electrical energy effectively, the material in question should have low thermal conductivity and high electrical conductivity. Such materials are classified as thermoelectric materials.

A low thermal conductivity ensures that the material does not easily transfer heat, which is crucial for maintaining a significant temperature difference between its hot and cold sides. This helps in generating a greater voltage. Meanwhile, high electrical conductivity is essential for facilitating the efficient movement of electrons across the material when there is a temperature difference, leading to maximal energy conversion.

Therefore, a material that optimally harvests heat energy into electrical energy should embody these characteristics.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : With the increase in the pressure of an ideal gas, the volume falls off more rapidly in an isothermal process in comparison to the adiabatic process.
Reason (R) : In isothermal process, PV = constant, while in adiabatic process $PV^{γ}$ = constant. Here $γ$ is the ratio of specific heats, P is the pressure and V is the volume of the ideal gas.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an isothermal process, $PV=\text{constant}$, so $PdV+VdP=0$ and

$\left (\dfrac{dV}{dP}\right )_{\text{iso}}=-\dfrac{V}{P}$

For an adiabatic process, $PV^{γ}=\text{constant}$, so $V^{γ}dP+γPV^{γ-1}dV=0$ and

$\left (\dfrac{dV}{dP}\right )_{\text{adi}}=-\dfrac{V}{γP}$

Since $γ>1$, $\left |\dfrac{dV}{dP}\right |_{\text{iso}}=γ\left |\dfrac{dV}{dP}\right |_{\text{adi}}$: for the same increase in pressure from the same state, the volume decreases faster in the isothermal process. So (A) is true.

(R) states the two process equations correctly, and these equations give exactly the two rates above, so (R) is true and is the correct explanation of (A).

The adiabatic curve is steeper on a $P$-$V$ graph ($|dP/dV|$ is larger), which means a given rise in pressure produces a smaller fall in volume, in agreement with (A).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A sand dropper drops sand of mass m(t) on a conveyer belt at a rate proportional to the square root of speed (v) of the belt, i.e., $\frac{dm}{dt}\propto \sqrt{v}$. If P is the power delivered to run the belt at constant speed then which of the following relationship is true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\frac{dm}{dt}\propto \sqrt{v}$

So, $\frac{dm}{dt}=k\sqrt{v}$ .... (i)

where, k = constant

We know, Power = $P=FV$

$\Rightarrow P=\frac{dp}{dt}v$ (As $F=\frac{dp}{dt}$ where, p = linear momentum)

$\Rightarrow P=\frac{d}{dt}(mv)v$

$\Rightarrow P=v\frac{dm}{dt}.v$ (As speed is constant i.e. v = constant)

$\Rightarrow P=v^{2}(k\sqrt{v})$ [From (i)]

$\Rightarrow P=kv^{5/2}$

by squaring both sides,

$\Rightarrow P^{2}=k^{2}v^{5}$

$\Rightarrow P^{2}\propto v^{5}$ (As $\mathrm{k}^{2}$ = constant)

Hence, option 4 is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in t minutes when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken by the similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at the same room temperature is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here, we will use the Newton's law of cooling.

We know, $\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\Delta t}=k\left (\frac{T_{1}+T_{2}}{2}-T_{s}\right )$ .... (1)

where, T${}_{1}$ and T${}_{2}$ are initial and final temperatures respectively.

$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{s}}$ = surrounding temperature

$\Delta t$ = time taken

$k$ = positive constant

Given,

Ist case :

$T_{1}=90^{\circ }C$

$T_{2}=80^{\circ }C$

$\Delta t=t$, $T_{s}=20^{\circ }C$

IInd case :

$T_{1}=80^{\circ }C$

$T_{2}=60^{\circ }C$

$T_{s}=20^{\circ }C$, $\Delta t=?$

Now, for Ist case,

$\frac{90-80}{t}=k\left (\frac{90+80}{2}-20\right )$ ...... (from (1))

$\Rightarrow \frac{10}{t}=k(85-20)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{10}{t}=65k$ .... (2)

For IInd case,

$\frac{80-60}{\Delta t}=k\left (\frac{80+60}{2}-20\right )$ .... (From (1))

$\Rightarrow \frac{20}{\Delta t}=k(70-20)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{20}{\Delta t}=50k$ .... (3)

Now, by (2) $\div$ (3),

$\frac{\frac{10}{t}}{\frac{20}{\Delta t}}=\frac{13}{10}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta t}{t}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{13}{10}$

$\Rightarrow \Delta t=\frac{13}{5}t$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A convex lens made of glass (refractive index = 1.5) has focal length 24 cm in air. When it is totally immersed in water (refractive index = 1.33), its focal length changes to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using lens formula,

For Ist case : $\frac{1}{f}=(a^{μ_{g}}-1)\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

where, $R_{1},R_{2}$ = radii of refracting surfaces

$f$ = focal length

$a^{μ_{g}}=\frac{{}^{μg}}{{}^{μa}}=\frac{1.5}{1}=1.5$

So, $\frac{1}{24}=(1.5-1)\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$ (As f = 24 cm given)

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{24}=0.5\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{12}=\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}=\frac{1}{12}$ .... (i)

For IInd case:

$\frac{1}{f}=(wμ_{g}-1)\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{1.5}{1.33}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{12}\right )$ ..... from (i)

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f}=\frac{17}{133}\times \frac{1}{12}\Rightarrow f=\frac{133\times 12}{17}$

$\Rightarrow f=93.88$ cm

$\approx$ 94 cm

Hence, option 1 is correct.

Match List - I with List - II.

  
    List - I
    List - II
  
  
    (A) Young’s Modulus
    $(I) M L^{-1} T^{-1}$
  
  
    (B) Torque
    $(II) M L^{-1} T^{-2}$
  
  
    (C) Coefficient of Viscosity
    (III$) M^{-1} L^{3} T^{-2}$
  
  
    (D) Gravitational Constant
    $(IV) M L^{2} T^{-2}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, Young's modulus, $E=\frac{σ}{ε}$

$\Rightarrow E=\frac{\frac{F}{A}}{\frac{\Delta L}{L}}=\frac{F}{A}\left (\frac{L}{\Delta L}\right )$

$\Rightarrow [E]=\frac{[F]}{[A]}=\frac{\left [M^{1}L^{1}T^{-2}\right ]}{[L^{2}]}$

(A) $\Rightarrow [E]=[M^{1}L^{-1}T^{-2}]$

(B) we know, Torque = $r\times F$

$[τ]=[r][F]$

$=[L][M^{1}L^{1}T^{-2}]$

$[τ]=[M^{1}L^{2}T^{-2}]$

(C) We know, $F=μA\frac{u}{y}$

where, F = force, $μ$ = coefficient of viscosity

A = area $\frac{u}{y}$ = rate of shear deformation

$\Rightarrow μ=\frac{Fy}{Au}$

$\Rightarrow [μ]=\frac{[M^{1}L^{1}T^{-2}][L]}{[L^{2}][LT^{-1}]}$

$\Rightarrow [μ]=[M^{1}L^{-1}T^{-1}]$

(D) We know, $F=\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}$ (Newton's law of gravitation)

$\Rightarrow G=\frac{Fr^{2}}{m_{1}m_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow [G]=\frac{[M^{1}L^{1}T^{-2}][L^{2}]}{[M^{2}]}$

$\Rightarrow [G]=[M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2}]$

Hence, option D is correct.

text:
[IMG]
Two concave refracting surfaces of equal radii of curvature and refractive index 1.5 face each other in air as shown in figure. A point object O is placed midway, between P and B. The separation between the images of O, formed by each refracting surface is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each surface has its centre of curvature at P on the air side, since $AP=PB=R$. The object O is at $OB=\dfrac{R}{2}$ and $OA=\dfrac{3R}{2}$. For refraction at a spherical surface, with distances measured from the pole and taken positive along the incident light,

$\dfrac{μ_{2}}{v}-\dfrac{μ_{1}}{u}=\dfrac{μ_{2}-μ_{1}}{R_{s}}$


[IMG]

Surface B (light travels from O towards B): $μ_{1}=1$, $μ_{2}=1.5$, $u=-\dfrac{R}{2}$, and the centre P lies on the incident side, so $R_{s}=-R$:

$\dfrac{1.5}{v}+\dfrac{2}{R}=\dfrac{0.5}{-R}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1.5}{v}=-\dfrac{5}{2R}\Rightarrow v=-\dfrac{3R}{5}$

The image $I_{2}$ is virtual, $\dfrac{3R}{5}$ from B in the air gap, i.e. $R-\dfrac{3R}{5}=\dfrac{2R}{5}$ from P towards B.

Surface A (light travels from O towards A): $u=-\dfrac{3R}{2}$, and the centre P again lies on the incident side, so $R_{s}=-R$:

$\dfrac{1.5}{v}+\dfrac{2}{3R}=\dfrac{0.5}{-R}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1.5}{v}=-\dfrac{7}{6R}\Rightarrow v=-\dfrac{9R}{7}$

The image $I_{1}$ is virtual, $\dfrac{9R}{7}$ from A in the air gap, i.e. $\dfrac{9R}{7}-R=\dfrac{2R}{7}$ from P towards B.


[IMG]

Both images lie on the same side of P, so their separation is

$\dfrac{2R}{5}-\dfrac{2R}{7}=\dfrac{4R}{35}\approx 0.114R$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
[IMG]
A poly-atomic molecule $(C_{V}=3R,C_{P}=4R$, where $R$ is gas constant) goes from phase space point $\mathrm{A}\left (\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa},\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}=4\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}\right )$ to point $\mathrm{B}\left (\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=5\times 10^{4}\mathrm{Pa},\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}=6\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}\right )$ to point $\mathrm{C}\left (\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{C}}=10^{4} \right.$ $\mathrm{Pa},\mathrm{V}_{C}=8\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}$ ). A to $B$ is an adiabatic path and $B$ to $C$ is an isothermal path.

The net heat absorbed per unit mole by the system is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As A to B is an adiabatic path,

So, $\Delta Q_{A\to B}=o$ .... (1)

So, now we need to find the heat absorbed for the isothermal path (B to C)

We know, change in internal energy

$\Delta u=mc_{v}\Delta T$

$\Rightarrow \Delta u=o$ (for isothermal as $\Delta T=o$)

Now, using Ist law of thermodynamics

$\Delta Q=\Delta u+w$

$\Rightarrow \Delta Q=o+w\Rightarrow \Delta Q=w$

So, $\Delta Q_{B\to C}=W_{B\to C}$

$=nRT\ln \left (\frac{v_{C}}{v_{B}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \Delta Q_{B\to C}=nR(450)\ln \left (\frac{4}{3}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \Delta Q_{B\to C}=450nR\ln \left (\frac{4}{3}\right )$ .... (2)

So net heat absorbed,

$Q=\Delta Q_{A\to B}+\Delta Q_{B\to C}$

$\Rightarrow Q=450nR\ln \left (\frac{4}{3}\right )$ ... (from 1 and 2)

Net heat absorbed per mole,

$\Rightarrow \frac{Q}{n}=450R(\ln 4-\ln 3)$.

Option 2 is correct.

Note: the printed data are not strictly consistent. For an isothermal path from B to C, $P_{C}V_{C}$ should equal $P_{B}V_{B}$, but the values give 0.08 J and 0.3 J. The result uses only the stated isothermal path, the 450 K from the figure and $V_{C}/V_{B}$, so the answer is not affected.

text:
A point charge causes an electric flux of $-2\times 10^{4}\mathrm{Nm}^{2}\mathrm{C}^{-1}$ to pass through a spherical Gaussian surface of 8.0 cm radius, centred on the charge. The value of the point charge is :

(Given $𝜖_{0}=8.85\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{C}^{2}\mathrm{N}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given an electric flux $𝜙=-2\times 10^{4}\text{Nm}^{2}\text{C}^{-1}$ through a spherical Gaussian surface with a radius of 8.0 cm (r = 0.08 m), we are to find the value of the point charge $Q$. According to Gauss's Law:

$𝜙=\frac{Q}{ε_{0}}$

Where $ε_{0}=8.85\times 10^{-12}\text{C}^{2}\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$. 

Rearranging the equation to solve for $Q$, we have:

$Q=𝜙ε_{0}$

Substituting the given values:

$Q=-2\times 10^{4}\times 8.85\times 10^{-12}$

Calculating this yields:

$Q=-17.7\times 10^{-8}\text{C}$

Thus, the value of the point charge is $Q=-17.7\times 10^{-8}\text{C}$.

A capacitor, $C_{1}=6μF$ is charged to a potential difference of $V_{0}=5V$ using a 5V battery. The battery is removed and another capacitor, $C_{2}=12μF$ is inserted in place of the battery. When the switch 'S' is closed, the charge flows between the capacitors for some time until equilibrium condition is reached. What are the charges ($q_{1}$ and $q_{2}$) on the capacitors $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ when equilibrium condition is reached.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $c_{1}=6μF,c_{2}=12μF,v=5v$

We know, for a capacitor $Q=CV$


[IMG]


Initial charge on $c_{1}.Q=c_{1}v$

$\Rightarrow Q=6\times 5$

$\Rightarrow Q=30μC$ .... (1)

when switch 'S' is closed, let q charge flows from C${}_{1}$ to C${}_{2}$

So final charges are $Q-q$ and q on C${}_{1}$ and C${}_{2}$ respectively.

Now, when equilibrium condition is reached potential on C${}_{1}$ and C${}_{2}$ becomes equal.

Hence, $\frac{Q-q}{c_{1}}=\frac{q}{c_{2}}$ (As $v=\frac{Q}{c}$)

$\Rightarrow \frac{Q}{c_{1}}=q\left (\frac{c_{1}+c_{2}}{c_{1}c_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow q=\left (\frac{c_{2}}{c_{1}+c_{2}}\right )Q$

$\Rightarrow q=\left (\frac{12}{6+12}\right )\times 30μC$ (From (1))

$\Rightarrow q=\left (\frac{12}{18}\right )\times 30=20μc$

and $Q-q=30-20=10μc$

Hence, $q_{1}=10μC$ and $q_{2}=20μC$

text:
An electric dipole is placed at a distance of 2 cm from an infinite plane sheet having positive charge density $σ_{\mathrm{o}}$. Choose the correct option from the following.

[IMG]
options: Torque on dipole is zero and net force is directed away from the sheet.
Potential energy of dipole is minimum and torque is zero.
Potential energy and torque both are maximum.
Torque on dipole is zero and net force acts towards the sheet.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The field of the infinite sheet is uniform, $E=\dfrac{σ_{0}}{2ε_{0}}$, perpendicular to the sheet and directed away from it.


[IMG]

The dipole points from $-q$ (nearer the sheet) to $+q$ (farther away), so $⃗{p}$ is along $⃗{E}$ and $θ=0^{\circ }$.

Torque: $τ=pE\sin 0^{\circ }=0$.

In a uniform field the forces $-q⃗{E}$ and $+q⃗{E}$ on the two charges cancel, so the net force on the dipole is zero; this rules out (A) and (D).

Potential energy: $U=-pE\cos 0^{\circ }=-pE$, its minimum value (stable equilibrium).

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 
[IMG]
 Three identical spheres of same mass undergo one dimensional motion as shown in figure with initial velocities $v_{\mathrm{A}}=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},v_{\mathrm{B}}=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},v_{\mathrm{C}}=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. If we wait sufficiently long for elastic collision to happen, then $v_{\mathrm{A}}=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},v_{\mathrm{B}}=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, $v_{\mathrm{C}}=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ will be the final velocities.

Reason (R): In an elastic collision between identical masses, two objects exchange their velocities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that two bodies of the same mass exchange their velocities after an elastic head-on collision.

Given, initially,


[IMG]


Here, $V_{AB}=v_{A}-v_{B}=5-2=3m/s$

$V_{CB}=v_{C}-v_{B}=4-2=2m/s$

first A will collide with B and the velocities will be exchanged.

i.e. now, V${}_{A}$ = 2 m/s and V${}_{B}$ = 5 m/s and V${}_{C}$ = 4 m/s

As $V_{B}>V_{C}$

So, B will collide and exchange the velocities with C.

So, $V_{B}=4$ m/s. and $V_{C}=5$ m/s.

Hence, finally,

$\begin{array}{ll}  & V_{A}=2m/s \\  & V_{B}=4m/s \\  & V_{C}=5m/s \end{array}$

So, A is false but R is true.

text:
A physical quantity $Q$ is related to four observables $a,b,c,d$ as follows :

$Q=\frac{ab^{4}}{cd}$

where, $\mathrm{a}=(60\pm 3)\mathrm{Pa};\mathrm{b}=(20\pm 0.1)\mathrm{m};\mathrm{c}=(40\pm 0.2)\mathrm{Nsm}^{-2}$ and $\mathrm{d}=(50\pm 0.1)\mathrm{m}$, then the percentage error in Q is $\frac{x}{1000}$, where $x=$ $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $Q=\frac{ab^{4}}{cd}$

$a=(60\pm 3)Pa\Rightarrow a=60Pa,\Delta a=3Pa$

$b=(20\pm 0.1)m\Rightarrow b=20m,\Delta b=0.1m$

$c=(40\pm 0.2)Nsm^{-2}\Rightarrow c=40Nsm^{-2},\Delta c=0.2Nsm^{-2}$

$d=(50\pm 0.1)m\Rightarrow d=50m,\Delta d=0.1m$

As, $Q=\frac{ab^{4}}{cd}$

by taking ln on both sides,

$\ln Q=\ln a+4\ln b-\ln c-\ln d$

Now, by differentiating,

$\frac{dQ}{Q}=\frac{da}{a}+4\frac{db}{b}-\frac{dc}{c}-\frac{dd}{d}$

So, maximum fractional error in Q is given by,

$\frac{\Delta Q}{Q}=\frac{\Delta a}{a}+4\frac{\Delta b}{b}+\frac{\Delta c}{c}+\frac{\Delta d}{d}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta Q}{Q}=\frac{3}{60}+4\left (\frac{0.1}{20}\right )+\frac{0.2}{40}+\frac{0.1}{50}$

$=\frac{1}{20}+\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{200}+\frac{1}{500}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta Q}{Q}=\frac{50+20+5+2}{1000}=\frac{77}{1000}$

Hence the % error in $Q=\frac{\Delta Q}{Q}\times 100%$

$=\frac{7700}{1000}%=\frac{x}{1000}$ (given)

So, $x=7700$

text: Two cars P and Q are moving on a road in the same direction. Acceleration of car P increases linearly with time whereas car Q moves with a constant acceleration. Both cars cross each other at time t = 0, for the first time. The maximum possible number of crossing(s) (including the crossing at t = 0) is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take both cars at $x=0$ at $t=0$. With $a_{P}=a_{0}+βt$ ($β\neq 0$) and $a_{Q}=a$ (constant), the acceleration of P relative to Q is

$a_{rel}=(a_{0}-a)+βt=c+βt$

Let $u$ be the relative velocity at $t=0$; $u\neq 0$ because the cars cross there. Integrating twice gives the relative position

$x_{rel}=ut+\dfrac{ct^{2}}{2}+\dfrac{βt^{3}}{6}=t\left (\dfrac{βt^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{ct}{2}+u\right )$

The cars cross whenever $x_{rel}=0$: at $t=0$, and at the roots of the quadratic in the bracket. A quadratic has at most two roots, and both are positive when $u$ has the same sign as $β$, $c$ has the opposite sign and the discriminant is positive.

For example, $β=6\text{m s}^{-3}$, $c=-6\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $u=2\text{m s}^{-1}$ give $x_{rel}=t^{3}-3t^{2}+2t=t(t-1)(t-2)$: P overtakes Q at $t=0$, Q overtakes P at $t=1\text{s}$, and P overtakes Q again at $t=2\text{s}$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Two planets, $A$ and $B$ are orbiting a common star in circular orbits of radii $R_{A}$ and $R_{B}$, respectively, with $R_{B}=2R_{A}$. The planet $B$ is $4\sqrt{2}$ times more massive than planet $A$. The ratio $\left (\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}\right )$ of angular momentum $(L_{B})$ of planet $B$ to that of planet $A(L_{A})$ is closest to integer  $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let a planet of mass m orbits a star of mass M in circular orbit of radius r with speed v.


[IMG]


For this circular motion, centripetal force is provided by the gravitational force between both masses.

Hence, $F_{C}=F_{4}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{mv^{2}}{r}=\frac{GMm}{r^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\frac{Gm}{r}}$

Angular momentum of the planet, $L=mvr$

$\Rightarrow L=m\sqrt{\frac{Gm}{r}}r$

$\Rightarrow L=\sqrt{GM}m\sqrt{r}$

Given, $m_{B}=4\sqrt{2}m_{A}$ and $R_{B}=2R_{A}$

M is same for both.

So, $\frac{L_{B}}{L_{A}}=\left (\frac{m_{B}}{m_{A}}\right )\sqrt{\frac{R_{B}}{R_{A}}}$

$=\left (4\sqrt{2}\right )\sqrt{2}=4\times 2$

$\Rightarrow \frac{L_{B}}{L_{A}}=8$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A parallel plate capacitor consisting of two circular plates of radius 10 cm is being charged by a constant current of 0.15 A . If the rate of change of potential difference between the plates is $7\times 10^{8}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{s}$ then the integer value of the distance between the parallel plates is $(~$ Take, $\left. 𝜖_{0}=9\times 10^{-12}\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}},π=\frac{22}{7}\right )$ $____________$ $μ\mathrm{m}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $r=10cm=\frac{1}{10}m$

$I=0.15A$, and $\frac{dv}{dt}=7\times 10^{8}v/s$

We know, for a parallel plate capacitor,

$c=\frac{ε_{0}A}{d}\Rightarrow c=\frac{ε_{0}πr^{2}}{d}$ .... (1)

In a capacitor,

$Q=CV$

$\Rightarrow V=\frac{Q}{C}$

by differentiating w.r.t. t

$\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{1}{C}\frac{dQ}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{d}{ε_{0}πr^{2}}I$ (As $I=\frac{dQ}{dt}$)

$\Rightarrow d=\frac{ε_{0}πr^{2}}{I}\frac{dv}{dt}$ .... (From (1))

$\Rightarrow d=\frac{9\times 10^{-12}}{0.15}\times \frac{22}{7}\times \frac{1}{100}\times 7\times 10^{8}$

$=\frac{198}{0.15}\times 10^{-6}$

$=1320\times 10^{-6}$ m

$\Rightarrow d=1320μm$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The magnetic field inside a 200 turns solenoid of radius 10 cm is $2.9\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{Tesla}$. If the solenoid carries a current of 0.29 A , then the length of the solenoid is $_______$ $π\mathrm{cm}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, magnetic field due to solenoid, $B=μ_{0}nI$

where, I = current, $n=\frac{N}{L}$ = no. of turns per unit length

$\Rightarrow B=\frac{μ_{0}NI}{L}$

$\Rightarrow L=\frac{μ_{0}NI}{B}=\frac{4π\times 10^{-7}\times 200\times 0.29}{2.9\times 10^{-4}}$

$\Rightarrow L=8π\times 10^{-2}m$

$\Rightarrow L=8πcm$

Hence, answer = 8.
